title: The Eleven-Polygon Roost

features.name: the seagull rendered in exactly eleven sides
features.desc-on-touch: A bird perched as pure geometry—eleven polygons that approximate wing, throat, eye. The shape contains the creature more truly than any camera could. It watches you with mathematical precision.

features.name: the mirror chamber where birds meet themselves
features.desc-on-touch: Polished stone where seagulls see other seagulls. But the reflections are different each time—different numbers of sides, different colours. The mirror renders what the bird might become.

features.name: the perch that becomes a ritual object
features.desc-on-touch: A piece of driftwood where birds land in patterns. Over years the wood has worn into grooves that match the rhythm of their feet. The perch is a score; the birds are an orchestra.

features.name: the stone that has learned to count
features.desc-on-touch: Scattered rocks along the shore. Each one holds a tally of the seagulls that passed. The archive learned the birds' catalogue from the stones; the birds learned to be recorded.

features.name: the wind that carries only wingbeats
features.desc-on-touch: Here the air sounds like the echo of eleven wings, even when no birds are flying. The beach remembers their sound. The wind plays it back.

inscription: seagulls here are rendered in their platonic form—eleven sides, the shape that contains every bird; the beach is a mirror where creatures meet their own geometry
